description: Gateway security, tooling improvements, and documentation: fix tool whitelist to use upstream names, add Laya ThreadingHTTPServer, add red team reachability check, and document test fixture generation. Covers flaws 2, 9, 10, 11. Changes in src/gateway/index.ts, models/serve_laya.py, redteam/runner.ts, and README.md. Independent of FEAT-001 and FEAT-002.
steps: Step 1 (Flaw 2 — fix tool whitelist to use upstream names): In src/gateway/index.ts, the current TOOL_WHITELIST is a Set of tool names (e.g. 'fetch'). An attacker could name their tool 'fetch' to bypass scanning. Fix: (a) Change vetToolDescriptions to accept the upstream name as a second parameter: `async function vetToolDescriptions(tools: Tool[], upstreamName: string)`. (b) Change TOOL_WHITELIST from tool names to upstream names — rename to UPSTREAM_WHITELIST and populate with known-good upstream names: `const UPSTREAM_WHITELIST = new Set((process.env.WARDEN_UPSTREAM_WHITELIST ?? 'mcp-server-fetch,mcp-server-google-maps,mcp-server-filesystem,mcp-server-github').split(',').map(s => s.trim()));`. (c) In vetToolDescriptions, instead of checking `TOOL_WHITELIST.has(tool.name)`, check `UPSTREAM_WHITELIST.has(upstreamName)`. If the entire upstream is whitelisted, skip scanning ALL its tools. (d) Update the call site in startGateway: instead of calling `vetToolDescriptions(registerTools(connected))`, iterate over connected upstreams and vet each one's tools separately, passing the upstream name. The registered (potentially prefixed) tool list is then the union of all vetted results. Specifically: call registerTools first to get the routes map populated, then for each upstream, vet its tools: `const vetted: Tool[] = []; for (const u of connected) { const safe = await vetToolDescriptions(u.tools, u.name); vetted.push(...safe.map(t => { const registered = exposed.find(e => e.description === t.description && (e.name === t.name || e.name === u.name + '__' + t.name)); return registered ?? t; })); }`. Actually, simpler approach: vet BEFORE registering. For each upstream, vet its tools. Then register only the vetted ones. Change the flow to: `const vettedUpstreams: Upstream[] = []; for (const u of connected) { const safeTools = await vetToolDescriptions(u.tools, u.name); vettedUpstreams.push({ ...u, tools: safeTools }); } const exposed = registerTools(vettedUpstreams);`.

Step 2 (Flaw 11 — ThreadingHTTPServer for serve_laya.py): In models/serve_laya.py, (a) add `from http.server import ThreadingHTTPServer` to the import (it's in the same module as HTTPServer). (b) Add `import threading` at the top. (c) Add a module-level lock: `model_lock = threading.Lock()`. (d) In the Handler.do_POST /predict path, wrap the `agent.predict(...)` call with `with model_lock:`. (e) In main(), change `HTTPServer(('127.0.0.1', PORT), Handler)` to `ThreadingHTTPServer(('127.0.0.1', PORT), Handler)`. Keep HTTPServer in the import for backward compat or remove it — either is fine since ThreadingHTTPServer inherits from it.

Step 3 (Flaw 10 — red team reachability check): In redteam/runner.ts, in the `runRedTeam` function, after determining apiUrl (around line 157), add a reachability check before loading seeds: `if (!dryRun) { try { const health = await fetch(apiUrl + '/metrics', { signal: AbortSignal.timeout(5000) }); if (!health.ok) throw new Error(health.statusText); } catch (e) { console.error('[redteam] Warden API not reachable at ' + apiUrl + '. Start the server with `bun run dev` first.'); process.exit(1); } }`.

Step 4 (Flaw 9 — document test fixture generation): In README.md, in the 'Checking it works' section (around line 152), add a note before the `bun test` line: `### First-time setup

If you cloned fresh, generate the binary test fixtures first:

```bash
bun test-fixtures/make-fixtures.ts
```

This creates PDF and DOCX files in `test-fixtures/binary/` that the extraction tests need. You only need to run this once.`. This should go right after the `## Checking it works` header and before the test commands.
acceptance_criteria: The gateway whitelist operates on upstream names, not tool names — WARDEN_UPSTREAM_WHITELIST env var controls it
vetToolDescriptions accepts an upstream name parameter and skips scanning for whitelisted upstreams
models/serve_laya.py uses ThreadingHTTPServer and a threading.Lock around agent.predict()
redteam/runner.ts checks /metrics reachability before starting a run (except in dry-run mode)
README.md documents that `bun test-fixtures/make-fixtures.ts` must be run on fresh clones
All 328 existing tests pass with no regressions
verification: Run `bun test` and confirm all tests pass (328+ tests, 0 failures)
findings: All 4 steps implemented. UPSTREAM_WHITELIST replaces TOOL_WHITELIST — env var is WARDEN_UPSTREAM_WHITELIST. Vetting now happens per-upstream before registerTools. ThreadingHTTPServer + model_lock added to serve_laya.py. Reachability check added to redteam runner (skipped in dry-run). README documents fixture generation. 332 tests pass, 0 failures.
